name: Used to and would
subtitle: Use used to + base verb for habits and states in the past that are not true now: I used to live in Leeds. Use would for repeated actions only. Don't confuse them with be used to + -ing, which means "familiar with".

flow.text: when I was young · every day

concept.exampleHtml: When I was a child, we used to visit my gran every Sunday. · She would make tea for us every time.

qa.html: Use used to + base verb for something that was true in the past, but is not true now. It can be a habit or a state: I used to walk to school. We used to live in Wales. He used to have long hair. The form is the same for every person.

Negative: didn't use to + base verb: She didn't use to like coffee. Question: Did + subject + use to: Did you use to live here? After did and didn't, the -d goes: use to, not used to. You can also say never used to: I never used to eat fish.

Use would + base verb for an action that happened again and again in the past: Every summer we would go to the beach. My dad would read us a story every night. First say when (when I was young, every summer). Then would is clear.
States (be, have, live, like, know, believe) take used to, not would: I used to have a bike. (✗ I would have a bike.) Actions that repeat can take both: We used to swim / would swim every day.
Do not use used to or would for one event, or when you say how many times. Use the past simple: We went to Rome in 2019. (✗ We used to go to Rome in 2019.)
Be used to and get used to are different. They are followed by -ing or a noun: I'm used to getting up early (= it is normal for me). I'm getting used to the cold (= it is becoming normal).

Typical mistakes: ✗ I used to going to school by bus. → ✓ I used to go to school by bus. · ✗ Did you used to play chess? → ✓ Did you use to play chess? · ✗ I would live in Leeds when I was a child. → ✓ I used to live in Leeds when I was a child.

concept.noteHtml: Used to sounds like "yoost to" /juːst tə/. For a finished action at a definite time, use the past simple. For habits now, use the present simple with usually, always, often. There is no present form of used to: say I usually walk, not I use to walk.

rounds.label: 1 · Past simple → used to
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence in the past simple. Say it again with used to + base verb.

example.answer: I used to play football every day.

items.prompt: We lived in a small flat.
items.answer: We used to live in a small flat.
She used to walk to work.
They used to have a big dog.
Tom used to play the guitar.
I used to get up at five.
Mei used to study late every night.

rounds.label: 2 · Negatives
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence with used to. Make it negative with didn't use to.

example.answer: I didn't use to like tea.

items.answer: She didn't use to eat meat.

items.answer: We didn't use to have a car.
He didn't use to wear glasses.

items.prompt: They used to live near the sea.
items.answer: They didn't use to live near the sea.
I didn't use to be shy.

exercises.title: used to only, or used to or would?
exercises.hint: A state (be, have, live, like) takes only used to. An action that repeated can take used to or would.

rows.term: We swam every summer. (a repeated action)
He called me every Friday. (a repeated action)
My dad read us a story every night. (a repeated action)
Priya walked to school every day. (a repeated action)

exercises.title: Choose the right form.
exercises.hint: Think: state or action? Positive or negative? Past habit or be used to?

items.prompt: Zofia ___ live in Leeds, but now she lives in York.
items.why: Live is a state, so only used to is possible, not would.

items.prompt: I didn't ___ like olives, but now I love them.
items.why: After didn't the -d goes: didn't use to.

items.prompt: ___ you use to walk to school?
items.why: It is a question about the past: Did + subject + use to.

items.prompt: I'm ___ getting up early now, so it is easy.
items.why: I'm used to + -ing means it is normal for me now. This is not a past habit.

items.prompt: When I was a child we went camping every summer. We ___ pack the car the night before.
items.why: The time is already clear (every summer), so would shows a repeated action in the past.

items.prompt: My brother ___ have a motorbike, but he sold it last year.
items.why: Have is a state, so used to. Didn't use to would say he never had one.
